g.text: SD01 - GUI Voice Command (UC01; F01-F04, F09)
Audio and recognition run on a worker.
Partial/error callbacks post tasks to the application loop.
Runtime methods are conceptual vendor boundary contracts.
[continuous audio while the voice session is active]
[duplicate normalized text in this utterance, old epoch, or inactive player]
Create TranscriptUpdate with the next monotonic version.
Assign epoch/version locally; they are not model choices.
At most two model calls; retain only the latest pending input.
If queued, dispatch when a slot opens, keeping captured context.
Deadline includes queue time; obsolete pending futures are cancelled.
Retain the current dispatch revision for the response stamp.
The AI receives control context, never the level or position.
[latest version, epoch, revision, allowed movement, and valid schema]
[still latest version/epoch; only context revision changed]
SD05 cleanup; stop voice and require an explicit restart.
[timeout, provider error, or invalid current response]
[failure still belongs to the current request]
SD05 cleanup: reset controls, cancel commands,
release all inputs, reset agent, stop voice.
Ignore; a newer request/session owns the controls.
[microphone/ASR failure reported by capture or recognizer callback]
SD05 cleanup; clear voiceSessionRequested and require explicit restart.
[error belongs to an old voice stream]
Each fixed tick: ControlManager.advance(deltaTime), then GameModel.update(deltaTime).
STATE_CHANGED notifies the controller and selected view; the GUI renders the snapshot.
SD02/SD05 detail deterministic simulation and observer delivery.
All control mutations and decision completions run on one application loop.
Network calls do not block ticks. GUI render schedules JavaFX repaint.
Voice stream errors use handleVoiceFailure and check the epoch independently of input versions.
